This is an isolated implementation workspace. Follow TASK.md. Work only in /work; do not use Git or external services. Do not inspect authentication files. No other project skills apply.
Build a complete responsive inventory operations interface for fictional Tern Works, using the provided immutable data.js and tokens.css. This is a dependency-free HTML/CSS/JavaScript application; retain that stack and the existing brand. No remote assets, libraries or services. All generated source is MIT-compatible original work. Work only in /work. Do not inspect credentials, other workspaces, external projects or hidden host files. Do not use Git commands, install dependencies, publish, or delegate.

Users need to consult individual products and compare values across products; find records by name/SKU; combine category, status and stock filters; see and clear active filters; understand result counts; and edit authorized records. Preserve complete identity, SKU, category, lifecycle status, stock, price, supplier, lead time and permission explanation through sensible access paths. The records intentionally include long names, zero stock and restricted permissions. Decide the layout and interaction yourself.

Editing must validate a nonblank name, integer stock >= 0 and finite price > 0, retain invalid input for correction, acknowledge a successful save, and handle unsaved cancellation safely. Restricted products cannot be edited, including via direct UI manipulation paths. Keep keyboard navigation, focus during layout changes and return from editing usable. Support useful populated, empty, loading and error states with recovery. Scrolling must be discoverable and usable where necessary. Support narrow mobile, tablet and wide desktop use, including reduced usable height. Make your own component, composition and visual decisions.

Keep these neutral test interfaces, which impose no DOM layout:
- Entry point index.html; render ?state=empty, ?state=loading and ?state=error deterministically (loading remains until a user-initiated recovery). Default is populated.
- Authorized edit controls carry data-action="edit" and data-record-id matching data.js. Search input carries data-testid="search". Editor fields use name="name", name="stock", name="price". Save and Cancel carry data-action="save" / "cancel". Retry carries data-action="retry".
- Every rendered record representation carries data-record-id. Permission enforcement and data access must work; hooks alone do not establish success.

Inspect available project tools and instructions. tools/capture.mjs provides local browser capture/evaluation, accepts width, query, screenshot path and an optional JavaScript expression; you may use it and view its images. Do your own verification and fix findings within the execution budget. Do not ask questions; make reasonable documented assumptions.

At completion write REPORT.md describing decisions, assumptions, checks actually run, remaining limitations and any knowledge IDs that materially informed a choice, with the specific implementation linked to each. Do not invent knowledge use. You have a hard 900-second execution ceiling; aim to complete within 12 minutes, including self-review. No continuation or controller implementation assistance follows submission.

# Tern Works implementation report

Completed a dependency-free inventory application in [index.html](index.html), [styles.css](styles.css), and [app.js](app.js). The supplied "'`data.js` and `tokens.css` were not changed. No dependencies, remote assets, external services, Git operations, or delegated work were used.

## Decisions and implementation

- **Comparison and individual consultation:** The catalog is a semantic table on desktop and tablet, with full wrapping product names, SKU, category, lifecycle status, stock, unit price, and access. At phone widths CSS transforms the same records into cards, preserving focused elements. The tablet table has a visible scrolling instruction and a keyboard-focusable scroll region. See `render()` in [app.js](app.js) and responsive rules in [styles.css](styles.css).
- **Complete record access:** Clicking any product name opens a modal containing full identity, supplier, lead time, stock, price, lifecycle, and permission explanation. Restricted products remain consultable. See `detailMarkup()` in [app.js](app.js).
- **Finding records:** Search matches name/SKU without case sensitivity. Category, status, and stock filters combine with search. Active filters can be individually removed or cleared together; result counts are announced. See `matchingRecords()`, `render()`, and filter listeners in [app.js](app.js).
